title: Use the lowest step that does the job
intro: Every automation sits on one step of the automation ladder. Compute, cost and CO₂ rise with every step, so start at the bottom and climb only when the lower step can't do the job.

steps.name: Rule
steps.what: A fixed if-then check. No AI involved.
steps.use_when: The answer is yes or no and you can write the condition down.

example.title: Invoice completeness check
example.how: A rule checks that the purchase order number, amount and tax ID are filled in, and returns the invoice if one is missing.
example.why_this_step: Checking whether a field is filled needs no AI. Only unreadable scans go to a person.

steps.name: Workflow
steps.what: A fixed sequence of steps across systems, triggered by an event.
steps.use_when: The steps are always the same, only the data changes.

example.title: Access request approval
example.situation: An employee asks for access to a tool.
example.how: The request goes to the manager, then to the tool owner. The account is created once both approve.
example.why_this_step: The steps and their order never change, so a workflow does it without AI.

steps.name: Classic ML
steps.what: A trained model that predicts or ranks from structured data. No text generation.
steps.use_when: You need a score, a category or a suggestion based on past data.

example.title: Ticket routing
example.how: A model trained on past tickets sorts it into one of twelve queues.
example.why_this_step: The input is structured and the output is a category, so a small model is enough.

steps.name: GenAI call
steps.what: One prompt to a language model that reads or writes free text. One call, no planning.
steps.use_when: Free text has to be read or written, but the task itself is a single step.

example.title: Personalised rejection message
example.situation: A candidate is not moved forward after the interview.
example.how: One call drafts a short personal message from an approved template and the interview notes. A recruiter checks and sends it.
example.why_this_step: Writing the text needs a language model, but there is nothing to plan or decide.

steps.name: Agent
steps.what: A language model that plans its own steps, calls tools and retries until the goal is reached.
steps.use_when: It must plan across tools or handle cases nobody can list in advance.

example.title: Incident investigation
example.situation: An alert fires on a production system at night.
example.how: The agent reads the alert, checks logs and recent changes, tries a fix from the runbook and re-plans if it fails.
example.why_this_step: Which check comes next depends on what it finds, so the steps cannot be fixed in advance. Record a one-line agent reason when you choose this step.

steps.name: Multi-agent
steps.what: Several agents with different roles that hand work to each other.
steps.use_when: Several departments each need their own agent and the agents must coordinate.

example.title: International relocation
example.situation: A new hire moves from Seoul to Walldorf.
example.how: HR, IT and facilities agents coordinate visa paperwork, laptop and access, and a desk and temporary flat.
example.why_this_step: Three areas with their own tools and rules have to plan together. This is rare: most cases fit a lower step.
